head_commit.message:
core: make shell behavior portable on FreeBSD

- Use /bin/sh instead of /bin/bash on FreeBSD/OpenBSD in the process group timeout test to avoid command-not-found failures.

- Accept /usr/local/bin/bash as a valid SHELL path to match common FreeBSD installations.

- Switch the shell serialization duration test to /bin/sh for improved portability across Unix platforms.

workflow_runs.display_title: fix: preserve assistant/tool call ordering in recorded turns

head_commit.message:
fix: preserve assistant/tool call ordering in recorded turns

commit cfcc87a95 changed how response items are batched and recorded, which caused tool call objects to be recorded before the assistant message content in some turns.

This could result in a { role: "assistant", content: null, tool_calls: [...] } message being sent before the actual assistant message with text content, breaking ordering expectations downstream.

This change reorders the items collected for a single turn so that the last non-empty assistant message is placed immediately before the first tool call object when both occur in the same turn, without perturbing prior history.

A new unit test ensures that recorded items now appear in the expected order: assistant text, then tool call object, then the corresponding tool output input item.

head_commit.message:
add deny ACEs for world writable dirs (#7022)

Our Restricted Token contains 3 SIDs (Logon, Everyone, {WorkspaceWrite
Capability || ReadOnly Capability})

because it must include Everyone, that left us vulnerable to directories
that allow writes to Everyone. Even though those directories do not have
ACEs that enable our capability SIDs to write to them, they could still
be written to even in ReadOnly mode, or even in WorkspaceWrite mode if
they are outside of a writable root.

A solution to this is to explicitly add *Deny* ACEs to these
directories, always for the ReadOnly Capability SID, and for the
WorkspaceWrite SID if the directory is outside of a workspace root.

Under a restricted token, Windows always checks Deny ACEs before Allow
ACEs so even though our restricted token would allow a write to these
directories due to the Everyone SID, it fails first because of the Deny
ACE on the capability SID

workflow_runs.display_title: Fix: Skip intermediate assistant messages between tool_calls and tool responses

head_commit.message:
Fix: Skip intermediate assistant messages between tool_calls and tool responses

This fix ensures that assistant messages appearing between tool_calls 
and tool responses are skipped to comply with OpenAI API requirements.

The issue occurred when intermediate assistant messages were inserted 
between tool_calls and their responses, violating the API's message 
ordering requirements and causing tool call failures with strict API 
providers.

Changes:
- Add awaiting_tool_response flag to track tool call state
- Skip intermediate assistant messages when awaiting tool response
- Reset flag when tool response is received
- Apply to FunctionCall, LocalShellCall, and CustomToolCall

Test Results:
- 100 tests passed
- 3 tests failed (pre-existing issues in official codebase)

Fixes tool call failures by maintaining proper message ordering:
assistant (with tool_calls) → tool (response)
